answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a scarce token before it may post jobs or claim rewards, with the lock rising for high-volume actions. A participant who proves fraud loses that stake through an on-chain slashing rule, while honest agents recover it after a dispute window. This does not make identities unique: an attacker can still create many accounts, but must tie up capital in each one and risk losing it. A fable, comet, or pearl earns no exemption.
